properties.description: Three suites. an_export_says_where_it_was_taken.rs (core, 4): the document contract — round trip, absence on an old document, detached HEAD, excluded from the content hash. an_export_says_which_tree_it_was_taken_in.rs (mcp, 4): a real git repository — branch and HEAD on receipt and file, dirty excludes the export itself, an unchanged design keeps its coordinate byte-for-byte across a commit, nothing outside git. test_reflow2_check.py TakenOnThisBranch (4): a modified export taken on another branch is refused with PHANTOM and exit 1; the same on its own branch passes; a committed one is not re-judged; one with no coordinate is not judged.
properties.findings: 4 + 4 + 4 passed. The chain, record-moved and auto-export suites and the whole gate suite (46) still green. One wrong turn on the way: the first cut of the write-path edit never landed on disk and three MCP cases failed with taken_at null; the instrumented rerun showed the reader was never called, and the edit was reapplied. The export_graph description had to be trimmed from ~1590 to 1470 characters to stay under the lint's 1500 budget.
properties.name: An export names its branch and commit, keeps them while unchanged, and the gate refuses one about to be committed elsewhere
